MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 12, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 7:20 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Eileen Hupp, President and CEO of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce led the
Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING NOVEMBER 30, 2019 AS SMALL BUSINESS
  SATURDAY

MAYOR MITCHELL presented a proclamation declaring November 30, 2019 as Small Business
Saturday. Eileen Hupp was on hand to accept the proclamation on behalf of the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that Item 5G (General Plan Advisory Committee
  Minutes of October 15, 2019) be removed for individual consideration.

  MAYOR MITCHELL requested that Item 5I (Planning Commission Minutes of November
  4, 2019) be removed for individual consideration.

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-F AND
  H AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 22, 2019 (CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING)

  APPROVED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 22, 2019

  APPROVED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OCTOBER AND NOVEMBER 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62110 THROUGH 62183 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $505,515.74; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100619 THROUGH 100719;
  11019; 62040 VOID (LOST IN MAIL) IN THE AMOUNT OF $102,110.60 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $607,626.34 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

E.  ENTRY GATE PROTOCOL AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB (RHCC) AND THE
  RESIDENCES AT RHCC

  APPROVED ELIMINATING THE OPERATING MEMORANDUM (GATE
  PROTOCOL) TO THE PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT APPROVED
  BY COUNCIL ON SEPTEMBER 25, 2018, THEREBY PERMITTING THE
  PROJECT GATES TO BE OPERATED IN A MANNER DETERMINED BY THE
  PROPERTY OWNER OR OWNERS ASSOCIATION.

F.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 21, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
 REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION:

G.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 15, 2019

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commented that it may be helpful to include more information
  regarding the Vision and Guiding Principles in the minutes.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN also suggested that the minutes include further
  explanation regarding Policy 1.4 and 1.6 referenced on page 3.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE GENERAL PLAN
  ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 15, 2019 WITH DIRECTION
  TO STAFF TO INCLUDE VISION & GUIDING PRINCIPLES WITH THE MINUTES
  (PAGE 1) AND FURTHER EXPLAIN POLICY 1.4 AND 1.6 (PAGE 3)

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

I.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 4, 2019

  MAYOR MITCHELL noted that the minutes reflect that several Commissioners
  expressed concerning regarding the size of the house proposed in Planning Application
  PA-18-19 and suggested that the City Council may want to discuss policy related to house
  size at the Policy Development Session.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 4, 2019 WITH DIRECT TO STAFF TO INCLUDE A
  DISCUSSION REGARDING HOUSE SIZE ON THE POLICY DEVELOPMENT
  SESSION AGENDA

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Ilias Stamos, 48 Ranchview Road addressed the City Council to suggest that the City Council
reconsider the Memorandum of Understanding regarding funding the School Resources Officers.

The CITY COUNCIL thanked Mr. Stamos for his comments.

A.  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON CIRCUIT RELIABILITY REPORT AND AERIAL
  SURVEY UPDATE

Vic Nol and Ryan Robbins presented SCE’s circuit reliability report for the Palos Verdes Peninsula
and provided an update on the aerial survey project including helicopter and drone survey
technology.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSAL FROM E.C. CONSTRUCTION TO REPAIR STORM DRAIN ON CLUB VIEW
  LANE

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to enter into a Public Works Contract
  (attached) with E.C. Construction (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney) to undertake
  the storm drain repair on Club View Lane, under the project supervision of Willdan
  Engineering, in the amount of $22,480 plus a 20% contingency of $4,496, for a grand
  total of $26,976.

  Community Development/Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the costs associated with project, including those to
  be borne by Rolling Hills Country Club. Further discussion ensued concerning the
  background and history of the original installation of the storm drain in the area.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO ENTER INTO A PUBLIC WORKS
  CONTRACT WITH E.C. CONSTRUCTION (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF
  THE CITY ATTORNEY) TO UNDERTAKE THE STORM DRAIN REPAIR ON
  CLUB VIEW LANE, UNDER THE PROJECT SUPERVISION OF WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING, IN THE AMOUNT OF $22,480 PLUS A 20% CONTINGENCY OF
  $4,496, FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $26,976.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PROPOSAL FROM WILLDAN ENGINEERING TO PROVIDE ENGINEERING DESIGN
  SERVICES FOR IMPROVEMENTS TO ROLLING HILLS ROAD AND PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council defer Willdan’s proposal for the Palos Verdes
  Drive East street improvement design services until Fiscal Year 20-21; and approve the
  Rolling Hills Road proposal (under the City’s Master Professional Services Agreement
  with Willdan Engineering) in the amount of $24,970, all to the satisfaction of the City
  Attorney.

  Community Development/Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
   In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’S inquiry, Director Wahba confirmed
  that the engineering proposal is for three design options at street view level.

  Discussion ensued concerning the timeframe for the engineering design services and the
  community input portion of the project.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, City Manager Grammer noted that it could be
  several years before the project would be completed given the reliance on grant funding.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested doing the Palos Verdes Drive East portion of the
  project first.

  Further discussion ensued concerning proposed design services and the soft costs
  associated with the project.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ, Director Wahba stated that it is estimated
  that a $15,000 budget adjustment may be necessary.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DEFER WILLDAN’S PROPOSAL FOR PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST STREET IMPROVEMENT DESIGN SERVICES UNTIL
  FISCAL YEAR 20-21; AND APPROVE THE ROLLING HILLS ROAD PROPOSAL
  (UNDER THE CITY’S MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING) IN THE AMOUNT OF $24,970, ALL TO THE
  SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: VETERANS’ MEMORIAL
  PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the installation of the Veterans’
  Memorial Dedication Garden at City Hall.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  MAYOR MITCHELL expressed support for the project noting that the individual that
  proposed the memorial was involved with the children’s games at the City Celebration for
  many years.

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL, Assistant City Manager Davis noted there would be
  no cost to the City for the original installation and the only future costs would be minimal
  maintenance costs with the intent of including those costs with overall campus landscape
  maintenance costs.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the City consider flying the Missing in
  Action (MIA) flag on the flag pole along with the United States flag.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ, Community Services Supervisor
  Morquecho confirmed that the donation for this project will go through the Pepper Tree
  Foundation, the City’s non-profit organization

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF THE
  VETERANS’ MEMORIAL DEDICATION GARDEN AT CITY HALL AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO RESEARCH INCLUDING THE MISSING IN ACTION (MIA) FLAG
  WITH THE UNITED STATES FLAG AT CITY HALL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

D  SB 2 PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM APPLICATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2448, authorizing
  application for and receipt of SB 2 Planning Grants Program funds.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) and
  reviewed a PowerPoint presentation explaining the SB 2 Planning Grants Program and
  the providing information on several of the new housing-related bills.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Planning Manager Naughton
  confirmed that the new housing requirements will exist whether or not the City applies for
  the SB 2 Grant funds and acceptance of the funds does not afford the State any additional
  enforcement mechanisms. Discussion ensued concerning the reporting requirements.

  Discussion ensued concerning the types of accessory dwelling unit standards that could
  be proposed in the City’s grant application package, should the Council decide to submit
  the application. Further discussion ensued concerning the impacts the new housing laws
  will have on the community.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2448, AUTHORIZING
  APPLICATION FOR AND RECEIPT OF SB 2 PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM
  FUNDS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
 CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis noted that his office will be busy over the next several months working with the
League of California Cities and California Contract Cities Association to address the recently
adopted State legislation pertaining to housing.

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that she attended the recent PV Transit board meeting and
provided a brief update on ridership.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that SBCCOG approved a letter of commitment with
American Dark Fiber and is moving forward with the South Bay Fiber Network project.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the California CCA annual
conference in Los Angeles noting that the sessions were very informative and the conference
was well attended and Rolling Hills Estates was recognized as one of the founding members of
the Clean Power Allilance.

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that the SCAG Regional Council met recently and approved the
Connect SoCal Regional Transportation Plan. She also noted that the Regional Council also
approved moving forward with Riverside’s proposal for the proposed RHNA allocation plan
although she was a dissenting vote on that matter.

MAYOR MITCHELL also reported that she recently attended the Cal LAFCO Annual Conference
where Los Angeles County LAFCO won a Best Government Program award for its Sativa Water
District program.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES ASSOCIATION
  SACRAMENTO LEGISLATIVE TOUR JANUARY 6-8, 2020

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE ANY COUNCIL MEMBER
  INTERESTED TO ATTEND CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES ASSOCIATION
  SACRAMENTO LEGISLATIVE TOUR JANUARY 6-8, 2020

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
 OTHER MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ reported that she and MAYOR MITCHELL attended the USC
Executive Education Forum. She noted that the program included very robust presentations and
discussion on very timely, pertinent topics. She expressed her appreciation for the City’s support
of these types of learning opportunities.

MAYOR MITCHELL echoed MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ’S comments about the USC
Executive Education Form and encouraged anyone else interested in attending to attend.

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that she attended a fascinating tour of Boring Company’s proposed
transportation tunnel.

MAYOR MITCHELL also reported that she, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ and COUNCIL
MEMBER HUFF attended the League of Women Voters Annual Reception.

MAYOR MITCHELL reminded Council and those present of the following upcoming events:
Promenade on the Peninsula Tree Lighting Ceremony – November 16; Parade of Lights –
December 7.

MAYOR MITCHELL also reported that the Prepared Peninsula Expo was very successful and
well attended with informative booths and interactive displays.

MAYOR MITCHELL noted that City Hall will be closed on November 28 and 29 in observance
of the Thanksgiving Holiday.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that he attended an event at Northrop Grumman on
November 4 to celebrate NASA’s historic James Webb Space Telescope program.

CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

ADJOURNMENT

At 9:50 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular City
Council meeting scheduled to be held on Tuesday, November 26, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the
Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
NOVEMBER 12, 2019
